extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians and mathematical researchers (authors, referees, evaluators), graduate students assessing mathematical work
extracted.subtask_description: A multi-axis rubric for judging the quality of a piece of mathematical work, listing distinct dimensions (e.g., problem-solving, technique, exposition) on which work may excel. Intended to be used to score, compare, and discuss tradeoffs across these dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good problem-solving
rubrics_metrics.description: solves a major previously-open problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognition for resolving important conjectures or long-standing open problems; often highly valued in fields like combinatorics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good technique
rubrics_metrics.description: develops or executes a virtuoso method that others can reuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates or refines methods and tools that become part of the community's toolbox; technique can be exported to other problems or fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good theory
rubrics_metrics.description: builds a framework that organizes a body of results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides unifying structures and concepts that explain and connect disparate results; often yields long-term influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good insight
rubrics_metrics.description: provides a conceptual shift that reorganizes understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offers a new perspective or way of seeing a subject that clarifies or simplifies prior thinking; conceptual reorganization can precede technical development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: uncovers an unexpected phenomenon, connection, or object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finding surprising structures or links between areas; may prompt new directions of inquiry even if not immediately formalized into theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good application
rubrics_metrics.description: contributes to another science or engineering field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mathematical results that have concrete impact outside pure mathematics; includes making tools usable by other disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good exposition
rubrics_metrics.description: presents existing material with unusual clarity, accessibility, or insight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear, insightful exposition improves dissemination and understanding; high-quality exposition is itself a valuable contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good pedagogy
rubrics_metrics.description: teaches others to do the work, develops the next generation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes training, textbooks, courses, and mentoring that enable new researchers to learn techniques and lines of thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good vision
rubrics_metrics.description: articulates a long-term direction or program (cf. Hilbert, Langlands).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enunciating ambitious, coherent research programs or conjectures that shape research agendas over decades.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good taste
rubrics_metrics.description: selects the right problems to work on, recognizes value early.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choosing problems or approaches with high payoff; early recognition of what's important is a form of intellectual judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good public relations
rubrics_metrics.description: communicates mathematics to non-mathematicians effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outreach, expository writing for lay audiences, and communication that improves public understanding and support for mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good meta-mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: clarifies the foundations, methodology, or self-understanding of the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work that examines the discipline's foundations, logical structure, or methodological assumptions and thereby improves how mathematics is done.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good rigor
rubrics_metrics.description: establishes results to the highest standard of certainty (especially relative to the field's norms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptional precision, careful proofs, and settling questionable steps; rigor is valued differently across subfields and eras.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good beauty
rubrics_metrics.description: produces results with strong aesthetic appeal in the Hardy/Poincaré sense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aesthetic qualities—simplicity, symmetry, unexpected harmony—appeal to mathematicians' sense of elegance and insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good elegance
rubrics_metrics.description: minimal apparatus, surprising compression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Achieving results with unexpectedly short, simple, or conceptually economical arguments or constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good creativity
rubrics_metrics.description: original ideas, unexpected approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novel lines of attack, creative constructions, or imaginative conjectures that break conventional patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good usefulness
rubrics_metrics.description: generates further mathematical work as a tool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Results that become widely used building blocks or instruments for subsequent research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good strength
rubrics_metrics.description: pushes a result to its sharpest form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtaining optimal constants, most general hypotheses, or strongest possible statements; improving precision and limits of applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good depth
rubrics_metrics.description: non-routine, non-superficial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Involves serious, hard-to-penetrate ideas or techniques; depth often correlates with long-term significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good intuition
rubrics_metrics.description: shows the underlying picture, not just the formal argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides heuristic explanations, mental models, or cartoons that help users grasp why results are true and how to generalize them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: introduces concepts that capture the right structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions that isolate the essential features of phenomena and facilitate theory-building and proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good notation
rubrics_metrics.description: uses or invents notation that clarifies (cf. Knuth on TeX).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notation that simplifies expression and thought, reducing clutter and making patterns visible; invention of useful notation can have lasting impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good organization
rubrics_metrics.description: structures a body of material so the relations among parts are visible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizational clarity in papers, books, or theories that shows connections and dependencies, aiding comprehension and further work.
